Aden, Sep 14: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighbouring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen's government.
The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast and one official conceded a “painful” defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
The escalation -- especially Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and its shipping in the Red Sea -- adds pressure on global oil supplies and prices, and that could give Iran leverage in its war with the United States.
As Yemen risks descending into another civil war, the United Nations estimated that more than 80,000 people in the impoverished country have been displaced by the fighting since the start of September.
One woman said a mortar shell fell nearby as she fled in the middle of the night from the town of Khawkha in Hodeida province along the Red Sea, shortly before it was captured by Houthis.
“I saw with my own eyes cars and buses burning, and bodies of children and women were lying on the road in a horrific scene,” said the woman, who spoke on condition of anonymity out of concern for her and her family's safety.
Houthis claim attacks against Saudi Arabia
Saudi authorities sounded sirens Sunday afternoon in the southern city of Abha and Khamis Mushait province, warning residents to take shelter from potential incoming fire. Both areas were repeatedly attacked by the Houthi in recent weeks.
The Houthis claimed to have used drones and missiles to target Saudi Arabia, including a military base just over the border with Yemen. Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree didn't provide evidence or say when the attack occurred.
The Saudi civil defence overnight said a projectile fell in a different area near the border with Yemen along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. The statement blamed the Houthis.
Saudi Arabia did not announce any new attacks targeting the Houthis.
The Houthis are targeting Saudi oil infrastructure and shipping as part of a recently declared blockade, but they have said they do not intend to threaten other countries' commercial shipping.
Yemen says 500 soldiers killed as it vows to fight back
The National Resistance, a government-allied force that had controlled coastal areas, said more than 500 government fighters were killed on the west coast over the past four weeks -- its first comprehensive toll.
It also said more than 1,000 Houthis had been killed in Hodeida and Taiz provinces. A spokesman for the Houthis didn't respond to a request for comment.
Yemen is home to over 40 million people who fear a return to the civil war that began more than a decade ago and killed 150,000, bringing many others to the brink of famine. Yemen's internationally recognised government and Saudi Arabia have been battling the Houthis for 12 years. A ceasefire that began in 2022 had mostly halted the fighting.
A senior government official in Yemen said its forces will return to the Red Sea coast and fight back. People fleeing the Houthi advance told The Associated Press they saw forces withdrawing and urging people to run.
Sultan al-Arada, a member of the ruling presidential leadership council, described the collapse of government forces in the port city of Mokha and elsewhere on Yemen's west coast as “painful and regrettable.” He said in the televised interview aired late Saturday that forces “are currently regrouping and will return to the battle.”
On Sunday, Rashad al-Alimi, who leads the presidential council, sought to downplay the defeats as “incidental,” according to comments published by the country's state-run SABA news agency. The government, he said, “will remain clear and fixed on the goal of retrieving (state) institutions and of reclaiming sovereignty over all national territories.”
On Sunday, the Yemeni military said it launched airstrikes on Houthi positions in Mokha, the coastal town of Dhubab and elsewhere in Taiz province. The rebels reported strikes by the Saudi-backed forces in Taiz province and artillery shelling in Saada province, a Houthi stronghold on Yemen's northern border with Saudi Arabia.
The advance puts Houthis closer to a major US base in Djibouti
The Houthis' advance puts them just 32 kilometres from the US military base in Djibouti, on the other side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. It's the main US base in Africa and one of several foreign military bases in Djibouti, including those of China, France and Japan.
The small Horn of Africa nation is already seeing the arrival of displaced Yemenis making the perilous water crossing. More than 2,000 Yemenis have reached Djibouti, the International Organisation for Migration said Sunday.
Djibouti's Economy and Finance Minister Ilyas M Dawaleh, said on X that the country's navy, coast guard and other specialized agencies were conducting rescue operations and providing emergency assistance.
Yemenis displaced by fighting worry about their survival
The UN migration agency said Sunday that more than 82,000 people in Yemen have been displaced since the beginning of September.
“The displaced people are in a very bad condition,” said Ahmad al-Masawi, the director of the Al Salam camp in the southern port city of Aden, who appealed to international organisations for assistance. “They left their homes quickly without any clothing or anything. They are crammed in camps, houses and even on roads.”
Hussein Haydara sat outside a shelter at the camp in a white undershirt, as his children waited to be assigned to a tent. He worried about how far the shelter is from schools, hospitals and markets, and wondered how they will survive the next weeks or months.
Haydara had fled his home in Hodeida once before, when the Houthis took it over in 2015. But this time feels more precarious.
“With the first displacement, we had time to plan things but this time we were forced to escape all of a sudden. One could hardly take their children and the lightest stuff possible,” he said.

CBS News says it needs to push “60 Minutes” into the future if the show is to survive, but the first telecast of the 59th season following a shocking overhaul of its on-air and behind-the-camera staff in May and June relied on many elements from the program’s past.
The new season of “60 Minutes” burnished stalwarts, and none of the new faces who have recently come aboard. Viewers on Sunday night got only a brief glimpse of Ross Douthat, and none of Sebastian Junger, Gianna Toboni, Trevor Phillips or Ariel Levy, but were rather greeted by three correspondents who already have an association with the program. Lesley Stahl has been with the newsmagazine since 1991, while Jon Wertheim joined the program in 2017. Norah O’Donnell was recently named a full-time correspondent on the show, but has contributed stories multiple times in the past.
Popular on Variety
One of the stories even featured the old-time TV-news “hidden camera,” which many people thought went out of style after ABC News got sued in 1999 — and lost — for sending reporters to take footage at Food Lion supermarkets after lying on resumes and gaining access to tape unsanitary food practices. ABC News got tripped up on charges of trespassing and fraud, and hidden-camera reporting in the modern day is typically used mostly in public spaces or overseas, where U.S. laws don’t apply.
Will viewers miss Cecilia Vega, Sharyn Alfonsi, or Scott Pelley? The last of that trio, all pushed out of the show following the decision to oust top producers, was on nearly every week, often crashing a story tied to events that had taken place in the days leading up to broadcast.
Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News whose work at transforming the unit for modern audiences has stirred up a lot of controversy, wants “60 Minutes” to show up in more media venues and kick up livelier discussions. Other members of CBS News have felt this way as well, wondering if the program has gotten too soft or overly reliant on stories tied to the release of new books.
There were no on-screen QR codes on Sunday’s telecast, or on-air prompts for viewers to join Stahl, Wertheim or O’Donnell for an interactive chat at CBSNews.com at some later day or time. There were no nods to listening to the stories via podcast. On Sunday morning, however, executive producer Nick Bilton sent out a note via email telling CBS News followers he would be publishing a newsletter every Monday that offered a behind-the-scenes look at the show.
Some of the window dressing has indeed changed. The opening logo is rendered more in black and white and has less red. The opening montage, which once looked as if spread out across the cover of a magazine, now looks as it takes place on a mobile tablet. One piece of the show did not change, at least in the first season broadcast. “The Last Minute,” a brief segment at program’s end that offers a few words about the program or its stories and was originally put into place by former executive producer Bill Owens., remains — perhaps because it has a regular sponsor.
The stories that were presented were segments that any longtime viewer might expect. O’Donnell nabbed an interview with one of the rescued Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran 34 days into the war (the segment was riveting due to its access to top military personnel, as well as the pilot, but did not offer any voice or analysis outside of the armed forces). Lesley Stahl probed the world of the so-called “pardon economy,” in which attorneys and lobbyists vow to win a presidential absolution for a convicted criminal — but don’t always deliver after they get cash (a nod should be given to The Washington Sun, the news outlet previously known as NOTUS, which interviewed one of the subjects of Stahl’s story several weeks ago). And Wertheim interviewed top personnel from the Los Angeles Rams. The show routinely tries to provide a mix of stories, one based on current events or an investigation, one focused on something overseas and one feature lighter in tone.
Bilton, who seized the reins of the show as executive producer earlier this year, may not want to shake things up overmuch in a season debut. Executives at CBS News, and parent Paramount Skydance, know only too well that “60 Minutes” generated $67 million in advertising in 2025, and saw its overall audience in the 2025-2026 season rise by 9%. Those figures will be critical for CBS News to maintain, especially as audiences continue to erode for “CBS Mornings” and remain below desired levels at “CBS Evening News.”
There are some differences, however, that the usual audience probably could not discern. Stahl’s investigation into pardons was a joint collaboration with “60 Minutes” and the CBS News investigative team, something producers at the program would likely have turned down in seasons past. Sachar Bar-On, a veteran “60 Minutes” producer, supervised the segment along with Michael Kaplan, a CBS News investigative producer and reporter. A person familiar with the show says “60 Minutes” will be “integrating more” with CBS News and its investigative unit, a move that provides more opportunity for CBS News rank-and-file doing this sort of work but also raises the specter of cost-cutting at a program with economics that already seem to work.
On Sunday night, “60 Minutes” put its best foot forward: correspondents the audience recognizes, and a story mix that doesn’t deviate wildly from the norm.
Keep an eye on subsequent weeks of the program. Weiss’ overhaul of the show interrupted a critical off-season period when correspondents typically try to file and finish a segment for the fall. Bilton and crew will enjoy a cushion thanks to having the new NFL season as a lead-in every Sunday for the next several weeks. Still, they won’t have the luxury of stories that may have been in the works for weeks, which may shortchange the amount of attention they can devote to segments from new on-air personnel who are still learning the ropes.

Six Nigerians accused of romance scams to be extradited to the US
- Published
South African police are handing over six Nigerians wanted in the US for alleged online romance scams to FBI agents later on Friday.
The group is accused of targeting over 100 women in the US and defrauding them of more than 100m rand ($6m; £5m), the South African authorities said.
Those being extradited were arrested in 2021 and are believed to be members of crime syndicate Black Axe - a Nigerian mafia-style gang tied to human trafficking, internet fraud and murder.
Some of their reported victims included pensioners and businesspeople "who were targeted through sophisticated online relationships used to defraud them of their money", according to South Africa's elite Hawks police unit.
The group will be "transported from a correctional facility in Cape Town" to the airport on Friday morning, where they will be "handed over to officials from the FBI and the United States Secret Service", Hawks spokesperson Colonel Katlego Mogale said in a statement.
They would face wire fraud and money-laundering charges upon their arrival in the US, she added.
- Mass arrests in global crackdown on West African cyber-crime networks 
  - Published25 August
Black Axe is a shadowy criminal network known for its extreme violence and operates across Africa, Europe and North America.
A BBC Eye investigation in 2021 suggested that the syndicate had become one of the most far-reaching and dangerous organised crime groups in the world.
Nigeria is its main recruitment ground and many of its members are university educated and inducted during their schooling.
The group has been on the radar of law enforcement agencies for a number of years.
FBI operations against Black Axe were launched in November 2019 and September 2021, eventually charging more than 35 individuals with multi-million dollar internet fraud.
Since then there have been several other operations across multiple countries targeting Black Axe co-ordinated by the global policing agency Interpol.
Last month, Interpol said during its latest one - which took place between November 2025 and June 2026 - seven sites in South Africa linked to a syndicate involved in romance and investment scams were raided.
It led to the arrests of 39 people, the seizure of money and the blocking of more than 250 bank accounts.

'Today the game was unprotected' - Arteta fumes but Arsenal survive
- Published
Arsenal's duality was there for all to see in their 2-0 win at Sunderland: gritty defence and moments of genius.
But things could have turned out very differently had a crucial 121-second period gone the other way.
After close to an hour of physical, full-blooded football, Sunderland were given a penalty when Ezri Konsa fouled Dan Ballard at a corner.
It proved the turning point - David Raya tipped Enzo le Fee's spot kick on to the post, and just over two minutes later, Arsenal substitute Bruno Guimaraes crashed in the opener off the underside of the crossbar.
Arteta's side left the north-east of England with their ninth successive Premier League victory. Not since the days of the Invincibles, in 2003-04, have the Gunners done that.
Yet Arteta was furious about the Sunderland penalty that could have cost his side.
"It's a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri [Konsa] does nothing. Just watch it," Arteta told BBC Match of the Day.
"We have a lot of cameras and VAR, we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing."
Referee John Brooks took a few seconds to point to the penalty spot after Ballard and Konsa hit the ground, but once he did the VAR stuck with his decision.
Konsa was certainly committing a foul, though Ballard did appear to have a hold of the Arsenal man.
"This should never happen, it's not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense," said Arteta, who was booked in the first half for repeatedly leaving his technical area.
"I'm making it very clear publicly because it's for the game, it's not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level.
"It's not acceptable, I've watched it 20 times and can't think of why it was given."
This season, Premier League referees have been instructed to clamp down on grappling at corners, something that became a big talking point last term.
"With the new laws trying to get rid of the grappling, Konsa is all over Ballard. You have to be looking at the ball," former England midfielder Karen Carney said on TNT Sports.
"Ballard was holding Konsa's arm but you run the risk," added former Arsenal defender Martin Keown.
"They want to stamp down on it so there is no point arguing about it."
However, Arteta was not alone in questioning the decision.
"It's absolutely not a penalty. He has got it completely wrong, Konsa's shoulder is pulled down by Ballard and he lands on top," former Wales defender Ashley Williams said on BBC Match of the Day.
"It's like a perfect toss in judo. It's very clever by Ballard but in no way is it a penalty."
'Magnificent' Raya and defence survive 'chaotic' moments
Though Arteta spoke more about the awarding of the penalty rather than Raya's saving of it, there is no denying that the Spanish goalkeeper's intervention changed the direction of the match.
The save - only Raya's second penalty stop in the Premier League - came at a time when Sunderland were putting the defending champions under pressure.
Though Le Fee telegraphed his effort, Raya had to be at full stretch to tip it on to the post. Until that point, the goalkeeper had largely been a spectator.
"He keeps us alive in the game, that unbelievable moment saving the penalty," Guimaraes told TNT Sports.
"I think after this moment we [took from it] a big confidence to play forward and score our goal."
"This penalty save is exceptional. He gets out so quick," former Brentford manager Thomas Frank - the man who signed Raya - said on BBC Match of the Day.
"For me he's the best goalkeeper in the Premier League and one of the best in the world."
After building last season's title-winning campaign on a stubborn defence, the Gunners have begun this season with five clean sheets in six matches in all competitions, including in all three away matches.
"It is a fantastic win and the ground work was done by the defence. They have weathered the storm and the goalkeeper steps up and makes a wonderful save," Keown said.
"He is very important to Arsenal and what they achieve. He was magnificent and doesn't get the credit he deserves."
Though seething about the penalty, Arteta took the opportunity during his post-match media conference to praise his side's defensive efforts.
"We knew we would have to go through some difficult and chaotic moments to have the right to win this game," he said. "But we have done it."
Guimaraes makes his mark
On a night when Arsenal were not at their fluid best, one hero was not going to be enough.
Guimaraes stepped up with a goal of the season contender, a curling effort from the edge of the penalty area.
The Brazilian midfielder has had a tough start to life at Arsenal since his £75m summer move from Newcastle, failing to start a match since the Community Shield.
Now recovered from a minor hamstring injury, he showed exactly what he can offer.
"That goal is about personality and character. It was him saying: I am going to make my mark at this football club," Keown said.
"He has been watching on the sidelines, but has said: 'Take a look at me - this is what I can do.'
"Boy did he shut the crowd up. A class player, going to the next level."
Of all the teams to announce himself against, Guimaraes chose the arch-rivals of his former employers Newcastle.
"It was a beautiful goal. Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle," Guimaraes told TNT Sports.
"But now I'm trying to create a new history here and I start with the right foot."
This match could have turned out very differently for Arsenal, but in the end, it was heroes old and new that got the job done.

The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours.
Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño, which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen.
But, as Ligin Joseph of the University of Southampton explains in The Conversation, its effects on India’s monsoon are not straightforward. A previous study in Science found that El Niño tends to bring more extreme summer monsoon rainfall to India.
This year, the southern state of Kerala has felt the brunt of the building super El Niño, with about a fifth less rain than normal. Yet intense downpours in the first week of August triggered flash flooding and landslides, killing 26 people.
The super El Niño is expected to peak after India’s monsoon season, but Indians are already keeping an anxious eye on the skies, wondering where and when the next deluge may come.

Prince Harry and Meghan's U.K. return gets a very British roast in Saturday Night Live UK sketch
The 4-minute bit took aim at Netflix deal, Markle's lifestyle empire and Royal Family tensions
Prince Harry and his wife Meghan's highly publicized return to England got the full Saturday Night Live UK treatment — and in true British fashion, the welcome was served with a distinctly chilly reception.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex were mocked during the Season 2 premiere of the late-night show on Saturday night.
The four-minute, 52-second bit took aim at, among other things, the couple's deal with Netflix, Meghan's television and business ventures, and the Royal Family's long-running controversies surrounding race.
The cold open began with Harry and Meghan, played by Jack Shep and Ayoade Bamgboye, visiting King Charles and Queen Camilla, portrayed by Larry Dean and Emma Sidi, at a sketch-set version of Balmoral Castle — the Scottish estate where Charles traditionally spends his summer retreat.
"Daddy, I'm home!" Harry proclaims to his father as he walks through the doorway. But the make-believe monarch seems less than pleased to see his son.
"Harry, what are you two doing here?" he scowls. "This castle is for royals only."
The fictional couple reveal that they are moving back to the U.K. "and need your help."
That sets the stage for Charles's withering indictment of the couple's finances and post-royal ventures.
"Don’t tell me you spent all your Netflix money already," Charles bemoans, referring to the multi-year production deal the couple signed with Netflix after they left the U.K. and stepped down as working royals in 2020. According to People, the five-year contract came to an end in 2025 after Netflix chose not to renew the deal under the same terms.
"Daddy, it was $60 million. How long was it meant to last?" Harry responded, drawing laughs from the studio audience.
Under the Netflix deal, the Sussexes produced several projects, including the wildly popular docuseries Harry & Meghan and Meghan's upbeat lifestyle and cooking program, With Love, Meghan.
Meghan used the latter Netflix series as a promotional platform for her lifestyle brand, As Ever, featuring jams, teas and honeys on the show. That, too, became fodder for Saturday's sketch, which didn't miss the opportunity to poke fun at her attempt to position herself as a lifestyle guru.
"Hey, step-queen, I brought you a gift ... it's ice ... I made it myself," the fictional Meghan told Camilla. "I'm kind of a whiz in the kitchen."
"It's true," Harry added. "She hires the best cooks."
Among the sketch's other biting moments, the writers appeared to reference Harry and Meghan's 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, during which they discussed controversial comments allegedly made within the Royal Family about what colour their son Prince Archie's skin might be.
During Saturday night's cold open, when Camilla greeted the couple, she began by saying, "Hello, sweet Harry," while kissing him on the cheek. Then, turning to the fictional Meghan, she said: "And beautiful Meghan, as brown as ever."
The segment then transitioned into a spoof of Britain's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, after SNL UK breakout star George Fouracres — portraying Burnham — burst into the room. The remainder of the skit focused on teasing Burnham's perceived obsession with being viewed as a "regular guy" while Prince Harry and Meghan ignored him and canoodled in the background.
The Duke and Duchess returned to the U.K. from the United States with their two children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, late last month. The family is expected to live privately outside of London.
No official reason has been given for the relocation. The couple's children have been enrolled in British schools and reportedly started classes this month.

- Defeating Kall Fimbulbringer will give players a Crown Jewel and Sacrificial Blood.
Valheim 1.0 update completes the game with the release of Deep North. This new biome features many new creatures, weapons, and secrets. It also adds Valheim’s final boss, Kall Fimbulbringer. However, summoning and defeating Kall Fimbulbringer is quite a task. So, here is a full guide on how to summon and defeat the Valheim Kall Fimbulbringer Deep North boss.
Valheim Kall Fimbulbringer Location
Before you can summon and fight Kall Fimbulbringer in Valheim, you will need to locate it on your map. As Valheim seeds are randomly generated, no two seeds will have the same boss location. To locate Kall Fimbulbringer, you will have to find his location runestone, ‘Vegvisir Aesir Passage’, which is also true for every other Valheim boss.
The Kall Fimbulbringer location runestone can be found inside Morkhalla, the new dungeon in the Deep North biome. This dungeon’s door can be found inside ruins in the Deep North, but opening the door requires an Intricate Key in Valheim.
Intricate Key in Valheim can be crafted using the Mould: Intricate Key, dropped by Elakings in the Winding Tunnels. Once you have the mould, freeze it inside the Frost Foundry using Bloodgold to craft the Intricate Key. Once you have done that, head inside Morkhalla and look for the Kall Fimbulbringer location runestone.
How to Summon Kall Fimbulbringer in Valheim Deep North Biome
Summoning Kall Fimbulbringer can be quite a hassle. If you want to cut to the chase and fight him without doing any work, simply use Valheim console commands. But if you want to fight him fair and square without cheating, here is what you need to do.
To summon Kall Fimbulbringer in Valheim, players need three 3 Malicious Blood. This item can only be obtained by completing Jotun invasions in Valheim Deep North. Players can start Jotun invasions by destroying the Malicious Ice found at the centre of Morkhalla dungeons.
Players will have to clear three Morkhalla dungeons, destroying three Malicious Ice, to mark three Jotun Invasion locations on the map. Once the Jotun Invasion starts, the location will be marked with a red circle on the map. Players will have to head to that location and fight off the new Jotun Invasion Valheim creatures.
After fighting the enemies off, destroy the Malicious Ice present there to collect the Malicious Blood. Now, head to the Kall Fimbulbringer altar in Valheim and use three Malicious Blood to summon him.
Valheim Kall Fimbulbringer Boss Guide
Kall Fimbulbringer is the strongest boss in Valheim and holds true to the title of being the final boss. He has three phases with three health bars, making the fight quite long and arduous. You will need the new Deep North Valheim 1.0 weapons and armor to defeat him comfortably.
How to Prepare for Kall Fimbulbringer Boss Fight in Valheim
Now, Kall Fimbulbringer has a total of 47k health, and he is resistant to the following damage types:
- Pierce
- Frost
- Fire
- Lightning
- Spirit (Immune)
This means that Slash and Blunt damage are the best ways to deal damage to Kall Fimbulbringer in Valheim. Also, for mages, the new summoning staff ‘Spirit Caller’ is extremely good against Kall Fimbulbringer.
Next, he deals a ton of Fire and Frost damage with his attacks, so getting resistance to both can be a lifesaver. Other than that, you need to get strong health and stamina foods.
There are plenty of good options for that, especially late game. But you can take a look at our Valheim recipes list to know which ones give the most buffs. You will also need a ton of meads to refill your health and stamina in fights, as the fight will take a long time to finish.
Finally, make sure to build a teleport portal near the boss altar, Aesir Passage, so that you can quickly return if you are defeated in battle.
How to Defeat Kall Fimbulbringer
With the preparations done, it is time to bring down Valheim’s “Shackled One.”
Phase 1:
In Kall Fimbulbringer’s first phase, he has 10k health and deals fairly straightforward attacks. Here are his attack patterns:
- Chain Slam: An overhead attack with one or both chains, dealing blunt damage. This attack is blockable/parryable, but don’t commit to attacking too much after blocking it.
- Chain Sweep: A sweeping ranged attack that can be hard to predict. Avoid blocking or parrying, and simply roll towards the attack at the last moment to avoid taking damage.
- Chain Whirl: A spinning attack that covers a large area around the boss. Simply run to the opposite end to avoid it.
- Chain Rush: A lunge attack that deals devastating damage. Avoid taking a hit at all costs. Dodging sideways at the last moment is the best way to avoid this attack.
In the first phase, don’t overcommit and simply do chip damage by waiting for animation resets or after parrying attacks.
Phase 2:
Kall Fimbulbringer is completely immune to attacks, and he summons a version of all the Valheim bosses. These are called aspects, and they perform the exact attacks the other Valheim bosses perform, truly creating a ‘final challenge’ setting for players. This is also a very challenging phase, as you need to defeat seven very strong enemies, with two fighting at the same time.
First, the boss will summon the Aspect of the Lightning Stag, which is the Eikthyr. Next, it will simply follow the game’s boss progression pattern. Here are the enemies he summons, in proper order:
- Aspect of the Lightning Stag (Eikthyr)
- Aspect of the Living Forest (The Elder)
- Aspect of the Writhing Dead (Bonemass)
- Aspect of the Dragon Mother (Moder)
- Aspect of the Twisted Soul (Yagluth)
- Aspect of the Crawling Matriarch (The Queen)
- Aspect of the Emerald Flame (Fader)
Defeating one enemy will summon the next, but the players will always fight two enemies at the same time. Players will need to defeat the Aspect of the Lightning Stag first, then the Aspect of the Writhing Dead. After that, prioritize defeating the Aspect of the Twisted Soul, and then the Aspect of the Dragon Mother. Finally, defeat the Aspect of the Crawling Matriarch and the Aspect of the Emerald Flame.
Phase 3:
This is the final phase of the boss fight, and this time Kall Fimbulbringer has 30k HP. The boss has a similar attack pattern as phase one, with some major differences.
- Elemental Damage: First, all chain attacks now deal elemental damage.
- Chain Fury: A new attack that deals rapid chain strikes in quick succession. Simply avoid getting hit and sneak in some damage once the animation ends.
- Tendrils: Tendrils sprout all over the boss arena, similar to the Elder boss fight.
Players will need to be very patient during this phase, dealing damage when they can, and avoiding everything else. The fight is mostly about who can survive longer, so try to save all your resources for this final phase.
Valheim Kall Fimbulbringer Boss Rewards
Once players defeat Kall Fimbulbringer in Valheim, they will get the following rewards in the game:
- Crown Jewel
- Sacrificial Blood
Crown Jewel is necessary for crafting the Crown of Valheim, which gives 50 armor, -20% Attack stamina usage, -20% swim stamina usage, -20% sneak stamina usage, -20% run stamina usage, and a 5% movement speed bonus. Other than that, it will also stop all Valheim creatures from attacking you in the game.
This is basically the equivalent of completing Valheim. Sacrificial Blood is also an end-game crafting item, making it highly valuable. One thing to note is that Kall Fimbulbringer does not give a Forsaken Power, and no item for any future progression. This boss is truly created to be the final Valheim boss.

One Facebook post with the story read, "Eric Clapton was lost inside a guitar solo when something in the crowd pulled him out of the music," directing readers to an article that started:
Eric Clapton Stopped Mid-Song for a Deaf Girl Who Could Feel His Music
Eric Clapton was lost inside a guitar solo when something in the crowd pulled him out of the music.
Twelve thousand people filled the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham. They were standing, shouting, clapping, moving as one body under the lights. The noise was overwhelming. The energy was electric.
And in the middle of it all, one teenage girl sat completely still.
It was September 23, 1992. Clapton was deep into his Journeyman tour, riding the momentum of sold-out arenas and roaring applause. He had already played through fan favorites, the band locked in, the night unfolding exactly as expected.
Except for her.
Third row. Center section. A young girl who wasn't clapping. Wasn't swaying. Wasn't reacting at all.
Her name was Sarah Mitchell. She was sixteen years old. And she was profoundly deaf.
Born without hearing, Sarah had never experienced music the way most people did. She had never heard a guitar string vibrate through air. Never heard applause. Never heard her own voice.
(Facebook user Youness ER)
The article further claimed that during a show in Birmingham, England, on Sept. 23, 1992, Clapton stopped midsong and brought a "profoundly deaf" 16-year-old named Sarah Mitchell onto the stage. Clapton supposedly positioned an amplifier behind her chair so she could feel the music's vibrations and then played a song for her as the arena fell silent.
Over the months, the story spread on numerous social media platforms, including X, LinkedIn and YouTube. Some posts featured links leading to articles on advertisement-filled websites.
Snopes readers also searched our website for information about whether the claim was true.
However, the story about Clapton amounted to fiction. Searches of Bing, DuckDuckGo, and Yahoo found no credible media outlets reporting about such an event, and several key details in the story conflicted with well-documented information about Clapton's tours and Birmingham performances in 1992.
The fabricated story resembled glurge, which Dictionary.com defines as "stories, often sent by email, that are supposed to be true and uplifting, but which are often fabricated and sentimental." It was one of hundreds of similarly fake stories about celebrities on Facebook that aim to generate views and advertising revenue via websites linked in posts.
Timeline doesn't match tour records
The story placed the alleged moment on Sept. 23, 1992, at the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham. However, Clapton's official timeline shows the Journeyman World Tour opened at the NEC on Jan. 14, 1990 — not September 1992 — and ran for three consecutive nights. Fan-compiled tour listings corroborated the dates and location. Moreover, the posts framed the alleged moment as part of Clapton's Journeyman tour, which ended in March 1991 and did not extend into September 1992.
Clapton did play in Birmingham in early February 1992, but those shows were at the National Indoor Arena, not the NEC. He later returned to the NEC for a series of benefit concerts in October 1992 — dates that don't match the rumored Sept. 23 appearance.
The story also isn't mentioned in "Eric Clapton: The Autobiography," first published in the United Kingdom in 2007. Because the book covers key moments from Clapton's career and touring life, the encounter described in the social media posts would likely have been included if it had actually happened.
AI-generated content helped spread story
The claim frequently circulated alongside an image showing Clapton with a teenage girl that appeared to have been generated using artificial intelligence. Hive Moderation, an online AI detector, determined that the image was highly likely to be AI-generated.
(Facebook user Dena Wells)
In August 2026, a nearly-identical image spread with the story, but this time with a black-and-white filter and a "Curiously Unusual Wonders" watermark:
(Facebook user Amila K Madige)
Similarly, most of the accompanying text was likely AI-generated, according to the AI detector ZeroGPT. (Research shows AI-detection software is imperfect. Readers should consider the tools' results with skepticism.)
(ZeroGPT)
The text's tone, structure and emotional language further pointed to AI authorship.
Finally, the story appears to have originated from a YouTube channel presenting itself as a source of "true stories About Eric Clapton that will restore your faith in humanity," but the video provided no verifiable evidence of the event. The channel's other content follows the same clickbait pattern, with sensational, vague titles and attention-grabbing thumbnails designed to generate clicks. Many of the thumbnails also appear to be AI-generated or heavily manipulated, which is consistent with a channel producing content that's primarily focused on generating views:
(YouTube channel @EricClaptonTheUntoldLegacy)
The false rumor about Clapton fits a familiar pattern of shareable, feel-good celebrity stories that spread quickly online because they appeal to emotion and usually rely on little more than reposts. We have debunked similar claims before, including posts alleging U.S. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump spent New Year's Day 2026 at a Pennsylvania orphanage and that Stephen Colbert launched a multimillion-dollar "Evergreen Sanctuary" for abused dogs.

Intelligence & resilience key in statement win for Maresca's Man City - Murphy
- Published
If you go to Old Trafford in a derby, go down to 10 men in the first 25 minutes and still come away with a 1-0 victory, it tells you a lot about your players.
Sunday's result was a statement win for Manchester City's new manager Enzo Maresca, who got his tactics spot on, but his team's performance will have showed him exactly what they are about.
I am talking about the mentality, discipline, organisation and energy you need in order to get a result when things go wrong for you like that in a game.
They were smart too, and that experience and ability not to panic goes a long way in football in situations like the one City faced following Phil Foden's early red card.
City are used to always having most of the ball but they were fine without it against United. That is down to leadership and communication - not just from the manager, but from the players on the field.
Maresca deserves plenty of credit for his decisions too, but he must be thinking he is a lucky man for having the group of players he does, because their intelligence and resilience was key.
As I said on Match of the Day, if anyone is doubting the competitiveness of City this season, just watch that game.
- Refereeing body admits judgement error over Haaland derby winner 
  - Published2 hours ago
- Foden sees red as Mainoo impresses - Manchester derby ratings 
  - Published5 hours ago
'City seemed to enjoy the challenge'
When it was 11 v 11, I thought United were the better team.
They pinned City back and were really bright going forward. Marcus Rashford, especially, was really positive and it felt like Michael Carrick's side were in the ascendancy.
The sending-off, which was the right decision by the way, kind of stopped United's momentum a little bit and also basically told City how they were going to have to play - they were going to have to defend for most of the game.
It is not what they are used to, but when you've got really experienced international players who are comfortable and calm, they don't really mind having to adapt.
They actually seemed to enjoy the challenge, and straight away they were well-organised and very disciplined.
United did not really create too much in the second part of the first half, other than a Rashford free-kick that hit the post, but I was thinking they would make a few tweaks at half-time and come out and really go after City. That didn't happen though.
'It felt comfortable for City'
United hit the post again in the second half, with Kobbie Mainoo's shot from distance, but they did not really create a clear-cut chance until Gianluigi Donnarumma saved from Bryan Mbeumo right at the end of the game.
Other than that, their decision-making in the final third wasn't great. They were shooting from silly angles or, when they got in some good wide areas and put the ball in, there were not enough numbers in the box.
United could also have changed their team around and brought on Benjamin Sesko earlier than they did, while I thought Rashford should have stayed on instead of Matheus Cunha because he was more of a threat.
But whatever United did try, City managed the game brilliantly.
Even at the time, I thought their winning goal really shouldn't have stood, because Enzo Fernandez impacts play and should have been ruled offside, but their defensive display was outstanding, and not just from their back four and central midfielders.
'Ndiaye gave City an extra dimension'
City were also superb further up the field. Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland were keeping the ball when it was played up to them, as well as winning free-kicks or beating people.
When he came on for Rayan Cherki, Iliman Ndiaye again did all of that brilliantly. He gave them a different dimension, and was a big reason they won the game.
That substitution was a clever one by Maresca and brave too, because while Ndiaye is better than Cherki defensively, he is also a ball-carrier who travels with the ball better too.
I remember Maresca making a couple of negative substitutions this time last year when his Chelsea side went down to 10 men early on at Old Trafford.
They ended up losing the game and he got a bit of criticism for it, but this time he went with Ndiaye, and it worked a treat.
He gave them an outlet and made some great runs - he was part of everything they did positively from an attacking point of view and was even involved in the goal - but also did his share of defending, and winning the ball back.
As the game went on, it looked like United were the ones who looked tired despite having the extra man for so long.
Maybe that was down to them playing on Thursday night, while City had their Champions League game on Tuesday, but it was not just energy that United were lacking.
They simply did not have the know-how to cause City problems. Let's not forget Donnarumma's late save because it was a brilliant stop, but Maresca's men were comfortable most of the time.
Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Donald Trump's backing for a united Ireland reignites divisive political issue
US President Donald Trump has caused a stir by stating his support for a unified Ireland.
The comments, made during a weekend trip to the Republic of Ireland, were striking because previous US presidents — even those with Irish roots, like Joe Biden — have avoided commenting directly on the subject of unification.
The issue remains a flashpoint within the UK and Ireland 28 years since the end of The Troubles, a period of civil unrest and violence over the status of Northern Ireland.
Here's what you need to know.
Trump makes his point, three times
On Saturday, local time, Donald Trump had a meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Dublin, and said they discussed various topics including trade.
Mr Trump afterwards said he backed Irish unity.
"Well, I don't want to cause any problems, but I will tell you, I'd love to see it unified," Mr Trump said.
"It's going to happen eventually … I think it would be a fantastic thing.
"Now the UK will have something to say about it … but I think it would be a great thing."
Mr Trump said later on Saturday that there "was no good answer" to the question on Irish unity but repeated that he thought it would be "a very cool thing".
On Sunday, Mr Trump attended the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg, western Ireland, and repeated his comments.
"You have Northern Ireland and you have Ireland and it would seem to me that one of the 'naturals' of all time is to put them together,"
Why have the comments sparked controversy?
After centuries of colonial rule, most of Ireland won independence from Britain a century ago in the Irish War of Independence, becoming a self-governing Roman Catholic-majority country.
Under the Anglo-Irish Treaty, the United Kingdom maintained rule over Northern Ireland, which was split between two main communities: nationalists — most of them Catholic — who desired unification with the rest of Ireland, and largely Protestant unionists, who wanted to stay British.
In the late 1960s, tensions exploded into The Troubles, three decades of violence involving republican and loyalist paramilitary groups as well as British troops and security services.
Over 3,500 people died, many civilians, in a series of bombings in Ireland and the UK, while British troops carried out violent enforcement, including the Bloody Sunday massacre.
Mr Trump's comments come weeks after new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said a referendum on Northern Ireland leaving the United Kingdom was "off the table", a position Downing Street on Saturday said remained unchanged.
Under the terms of the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, the accord that largely ended 30 years of conflict, a referendum can be held only at the discretion of the British government.
How have politicians reacted?
Gavin Robinson, the leader of the Democratic Unionist Party, Northern Ireland's largest party advocating continued union with Britain, wrote on X:
"Northern Ireland's constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.
"Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom because that is the settled democratic will of its people."
Sinn Féin, a political party that supports the unification of Ireland, said it approved of Mr Trump's comments, although the left-leaning party has little in common with him politically.
Gerry Adams who was Sinn Féin leader when the Good Friday accord was signed, said:
The "remarks by President Trump on the issue of Irish unity are welcome, even though we profoundly differ with him on many other matters."
Andy Burnham's office pointed back to his statement last week that he was "100 per cent" behind the Good Friday accord and that the UK would only consider allowing a referendum "when public opinion has changed to the point where the call has to be considered".
Opposition UK Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said Mr Trump was "shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state".
"This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension."
Donald Trump has repeatedly spoken of plans to make Canada the "51st state" of the US, and angered authorities in Greenland by suggesting he could launch a takeover of the country.
Will Trump weigh in on Scotland next?
Mr Trump was asked on Sunday about independence for Scotland.
"You asked about Scotland. That one I won't talk about yet. I'll save that for another day," he said.
Scotland held a referendum in 2014 in which the population narrowly voted to remain part of Britain. Governments since have ruled out an immediate re-run.
In a separate development, the leaders of the main Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish separatist parties announced in a statement that they were to hold talks in Cardiff on Monday, local time, aiming to advance their campaigns to break away from Britain.

Mumbai Police deny nod for activist Manoj Jarange's September 19 hunger strike at Azad Maidan
The cops, while rejecting Jarange-Patil's formal request, cited potential security concerns owing to the ongoing Ganeshotsav festival.
The Mumbai Police on Sunday denied permission to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil for his indefinite hunger strike from September 19 at the Azad Maidan.
The cops, while rejecting Jarange-Patil's formal request, cited potential security concerns owing to the ongoing Ganeshotsav festival, PTI news agency reported.
This came even as Jarange-Patil, who hunger strike entered its 16th day on Sunday, alleged that there was a plot to kill him and cause unrest during his planned 'peaceful' march to Mumbai over the Maratha reservation issue. The activist had called for a march from September 14 to September 25.
Jarange-Patil slammed the police's decision, accusing the Maharashtra government of attempting to suppress his agitation. While speaking in Antarwali Sarati in Jalna, he claimed the act went against the directives of the Bombay High Court, terming it as dictatorship and high-handedness. “Why do they (government and police) assume we will violate the rules before the protest even begins? Under what law is this government functioning?” he questioned, while saying his legal team would challenge the police order, PTI reported.
Mumbai Police issues six-page refusal letter, cites previous non-compliance issues
Issuing a six-page refusal letter, Azad Maidan police station senior inspector Raja Bidkar turned down the activist's request. The letter, apart from the Ganeshotsav festivities, also cited potential violations of Public Meetings, Demonstrations, and Processions Rules.
It further alleged non-compliance with venue conditions during the previous protests led by Jarange-Patil, according to the PTI report. They mentioned the huge crowds during last year's stir, which had exceeded permitted limits. This had also resulted in traffic disruptions around Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters.
Apart from these reasons, officials said the deployment of forces was stretched because of crowds expected for Ganpati festivities, and permitting a large demonstration during this time could trigger a law and order situation, PTI reported. They added that despite assurances extended by Jarange-Patil, a nod to the march would pose significant operational risks.
Jarange-Patil's ‘conspiracy’ allegation
Jarange-Patil has alleged that people linked to the ruling parties could be sent into the march to cause disorder and attack him. "There is a conspiracy to shoot me during the march. They do not want to kill Marathas, but want to target me,” he alleged.
He made the claim while speaking to supporters and media persons at the protest site in Maharashtra's Jalna district. "I will accept death, but I will not surrender," he said, adding that the state government had eight days to settle the matter before the planned protest march in Mumbai.

Turkish authorities launch crackdown on LGBTQ+ and HIV support groups
Turkish authorities have cracked down on multiple LGBTQ+ groups and individuals, detaining dozens and raiding association offices and popular hangouts
ISTANBUL -- Turkish authorities cracked down on multiple LGBTQ+ groups and individuals early Sunday morning, detaining dozens of members, breaking into association offices and raiding popular hangouts.
In an escalation of its decade-long hostility toward LGBTQ+ groups, particularly in the lead-up to elections, simultaneous police raids beginning at 1 a.m. took place in the major cities of Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin and Mersin.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced on social media that the investigation into 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses was to “protect children, the institution of the family, and public order” in line with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s 10-year executive order relating to families and children.
“As per the duty to protect families and children given to the state by the constitution, no criminal organization, abuse network or illegal activity which targets children, youths or families will be tolerated!” Gurlek said.
The raids targeted both current and former members of multiple prominent LGBTQ+ rights and HIV awareness groups. The organizations’ websites were also blocked.
Gurlek also noted that such associations were found to receive significant funding from international sources and agencies.
The Human Rights Association condemned the raids. “This is not a judicial investigation; it is a political operation aimed at forcing society into a monolithic family model and purging LGBTI+ and independent civil society under the guise of protecting the family and children," it said.
"To include unrelated charges such as ‘forming a criminal organization,’ ‘drugs,’ ‘prostitution’ and ‘obscenity’ serves not to reveal the truth but to incriminate the entire community.”
The religious conservative Justice and Development Party has been increasingly vocal against LGBTQ+ groups to play up to the more conservative elements of its base. In 2015, it banned Istanbul Pride, which had tens of thousands of attendees in previous years prior. Since then, authorities have violently dispersed any attempted gatherings for Pride.
This summer, an LGBTQ+ cruise ship that tours the Mediterranean and has docked in Turkey multiple times in the past was refused permission to dock there.
The Ottoman Empire, predecessor to the modern republic of Turkey, decriminalized homosexuality in 1858, however there is still significant social discrimination.

Months after Turning Point USA CEO Charlie Kirk was fatally shot on Sept. 10, 2025, a rumor circulated online that his widow, Erika Kirk, had announced she was pregnant shortly after her husband's death.
The claim about her supposed pregnancy resurfaced (archived) about a year after Kirk's killing, with many people online noting that the baby should have been born by then.
Some social media users speculated it was an example of the "Mandela Effect" — a phenomenon that occurs when people collectively misremember reality.
"Wait wasn't erika kirk supposed to be pregnant or is that some kind of mandela effect?" one TikTok user asked in July 2026. The post (archived), which received more than 4.2 million views as of this writing, was captioned: "It's been well over 9 months."
Dozens of Snopes readers searched searched the site for answers.
While Erika Kirk has repeatedly talked about the two children she had with Charlie Kirk, there's no evidence that she announced she was pregnant again after her husband was assassinated. The rumor has persisted since the shooting took place. We first looked into it in September 2025 and found no evidence that it was true.
In November 2025, during an interview with conservative commentator Megyn Kelly, Erika Kirk said that she and Charlie Kirk had wanted four children.
"I was praying to God that I was pregnant when he got murdered," she said. "I was like, oh goodness, that would be the ultimate blessing out of this catastrophe."
She did not confirm she was pregnant at any point during the interview.
Despite dozens of false claims — often generated using artificial intelligence tools — that Erika Kirk announced she was pregnant after her husband died, Snopes found no evidence in publicly available sources that she made such an announcement.
For further reading, we previously investigated claims that Erika Kirk lost her children in a custody battle and that she had an affair with U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

A federal judge late Sunday (September 13, 2026) ordered that the U.S. Postal Service not implement U.S. President Donald Trump’s executive order limiting mail balloting, adding another obstacle to the administration’s effort to rewrite election rules as the Supreme Court is poised to weigh in on the matter.
The nation’s highest court is already considering the administration’s appeal of an order by U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani in Boston prohibiting the Postal Service from enforcing its new rule on mail voting before this year’s midterm elections.
Late Sunday (September 13), U.S. District Judge Carl J. Nichols in Washington, D.C., handed down a similar hold on the rule, which was issued on August 21.
“Plaintiffs have demonstrated that, absent an injunction, there is an increased risk that a significant number of otherwise appropriate absentee or mail-in ballots will ultimately not be counted in the upcoming elections,” Mr. Nichols wrote in issuing the preliminary injunction.
“The public has a strong interest in ensuring that doesn’t happen.”
Mr. Nichols in May had refused to issue an injunction because he ruled the lawsuit seeking one was brought too early. That was the high court’s reasoning late last month when it lifted an earlier freeze by Ms. Talwani. But because the administration had just issued its rule to move ahead with Mr. Trump’s plan, the plaintiffs in Boston and Washington, D.C., refiled their lawsuits.
Ms. Talwani was nominated by former President Barack Obama and Mr. Nichols was nominated by Mr. Trump.
The new Postal Service regulations stem from an executive order Mr. Trump issued earlier this year. Election officials say it would be impossible to implement the changes this close to a general election.
The regulations would require all ballot envelope designs to be pre-approved by the Postal Service and that states upload the identities of those who are to receive them into a still-inactive online portal. Mail ballots already are being sent out in at least three states — Alabama, North Carolina and Wisconsin — and more states are preparing to distribute mail ballots this week.
A whistleblower report to Congress warned that millions of people would be disenfranchised if the rule were allowed to take effect for the midterms. The union representing U.S. Postal Service workers has pushed back against the executive order, saying it is not the job of postal workers to verify voter eligibility.
Mail balloting has long been a favorite target for Mr. Trump, who has falsely blamed it for his 2020 loss to Democrat Joe Biden and claimed it is a pathway to fraud despite his own use of the voting method.

Mario-a-Lago Kart, Anyone?
The White House made a bunch of parody video games. We have more suggestions.
This week, the White House removed a Tetris-inspired game called Build the Wall from its recently launched arcade website after the Tetris Company publicly warned that it takes copyright law “very seriously.”
Here are a few options the White House might consider to replace the game:
Super PAC-Man
Players direct a round creature with a constantly moving mouth through a maze as he munches on tiny coins. Meanwhile, the ghosts of financial lawsuits past pursue Super PAC-Man—but consuming excerpts from favorable Supreme Court rulings allows him to temporarily devour these ghosts, too. Once Super PAC-Man collects all the coins, he progresses, unsatiated, to the next level, where he sends out a single text and all the money starts flowing directly toward him.
Words With Enemies
Players form new, hateful attacks in this Scrabble-like multiplayer game using letters cut from public-school textbooks, removed museum displays, and maps depicting the former Lake Ontario. Highest-scoring insults include: SCUZZY, ZANY, and LOW-IQ JOKER. Extra points are awarded for letters placed on various Random Capitalization Squares.
Mario-a-Lago Kart
Up to four players race golf carts around a cartoonishly decorated beach club, crashing through boxes of classified documents to unlock power-ups including nuclear footballs and black markers for unlimited redactions. Between races, players can refuel at the gas pump, assuming they have collected the requisite 175,000 coins per gallon. The winner receives a golf trophy; second, third, and fourth place—as well as any observers or people simply standing nearby—get access to state secrets.
Grand Theft Crypto
This game is all in the timing: Players must market their own cryptocurrency, then wait until just the right moment to cash out, crashing the currency and tanking other players’ life savings.
The Oregon Data Center
Modern-day pioneers move into a covered wagon after an eminent-domain order for the construction of a data center displaces them from their hometown. Drinking water is scarce, noise pollution is earsplitting, and morale is low as players try to survive the perilous journey to one of the few remaining corners of protected parkland. Inevitably, all players die when artificial general intelligence bioengineers a new form of dysentery.
Goldeneye
In this first-person interior-design game, players gild every nook, cranny, and free patch of wall space in their virtual home office.
Coal Minecraft
No longer beholden to child-labor regulations, players ages 6 to 8 design their own pickaxes before descending 1,500 feet down a shaft to mine bituminous coal. Open-world play means that the only limit is kids’ imagination and black lung and tunnel collapse.
Super Smash the Kennedy Center
Players battle conservationists, historians, and patrons of the arts atop a revered memorial building, destroying it in the process. Downloadable content expands play to the Reflecting Pool, the National Mall, and the East Wing of the White House.
Candy Crush the American Dream
Players rearrange foods that were once safe to eat into matching groups to make them disappear as part of an FDA recall. But miss just one, and players will contract a parasitic infection that sends them to the hospital, where they will incur astronomical medical bills, which will prevent them from qualifying for a mortgage, which will force them to move back in with their parents.
President Evil
A zombie occupies the most powerful office in the world. At the conclusion of Level 2, President Evil might insist that the game isn’t over, but so long as it works as intended, someone else will finally get a turn to play.

Data from Greater Bay Area’s 88 million residents to help improve healthcare policy: GSK
Executive says pharmaceutical company is investing in shared data infrastructure
GSK Hong Kong and Macau general manager Nicholas Teo said patient data was very important because it could form “supplementary evidence” to support regulatory filings and potential label expansions, and also help to “discover benefits other than the medication itself”.
Vaccines were one example, Teo said last week. While their effectiveness against target diseases such as flu, shingles and respiratory syncytial virus was well established, he said researchers were increasingly studying potential benefits relating to cardiovascular health and neurological outcomes, which might help generate additional evidence and insights for future healthcare decision-making.
Teo said GSK’s expertise lay in vaccination and disease prevention, citing shingles and respiratory syncytial virus as key areas, with the viral liver infection hepatitis B another area of focus. He added that GSK also had a growing oncology and haematology portfolio.
The bay area is a Chinese government scheme aimed at integrating Hong Kong, Macau and nine cities in mainland China’s Guangdong province into a single economic and business hub. Their combined gross domestic product last year was more than US$2.23 trillion, according to official data.
Teo said GSK would provide financial sponsorship for the HKU-led study and was also investing in shared data infrastructure. The company could access patient data through the partnership, such as data coming from hospitals and government agencies, but pharmaceutical companies did not have direct access to it on their own, he added.

This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Camila Valim. It has been edited for length and clarity.
I spent two decades in corporate as head of marketing for an entertainment group. I left that job due to burnout. I pivoted to becoming a professional organizer and started a successful Instagram account and business.
Then I got divorced five years ago and had to return to the corporate world.
I went back to what I knew, working as a marketing consultant. My contract ended eight months ago. I expected it, but the job search to find a new marketing client has been tough.
I've only had 2 interviews
In eight months, I've only had two interviews. I've been carrying my whole household as a single parent and sole provider for two kids, ages 9 and 12.
I got very far in an interview process a few weeks ago for a head of brand and communications position. It felt like my last lifeline. I told myself, "OK, when I get this job, I'll be able to keep my lifestyle as it is; I won't have to sell my house." I was picking my kids up at school when I got the call that they loved me, but someone else got the job.
I knew then I had to make really serious decisions and take steps that weren't going to be fun.
My food delivery job is flexible
A cousin suggested I do meal deliveries on my e-bike while I searched for a new corporate job.
The process was very quick, and I got approved to deliver in no time. It's flexible and fits with my single-parent schedule. I can be there for my kids, still look for a job in corporate, and create content and rebuild my organizing business at once.
I've learned a lot on the bike, such as punctuality in a way I've never had to deal with before. I'm bringing food and smiles to people at their doors, and I love the freedom of being on the bike. It's a rush, and it gives me time to think. I have lots of insights and ideas on the bike.
The freedom has helped me create healthy space in my mind and take my creativity places it hasn't been before. For example, while on the bike, I had the idea to print out my story and CV and hand them out to people. I deliver to a lot of people who work for big businesses.
I will take income in any form I can get and do whatever it takes. I'm working on growing my Instagram account again. I know I have to sell my house, but I'm grateful I have it as a backup plan to put more money on the table to put food on the table.
I think people recognize themselves in me
This is a bridge for me until my house sells. I cannot live off of delivering food, and I am still pursuing the next chapter of my career.
I posted an Instagram reel about how this is not how I saw life at 45. It went viral. It has almost 900,000 views. I think it went viral because I was refusing to feel ashamed, and I hopefully gave other people permission to stop feeling ashamed, too.
I expected it to resonate with women, but it resonated with men as well. I have women and men messaging me, saying they've never told anyone they're in the same position. I think that tells you how much silence there is around this for everyone.

Civic bodies must give seizure details of vendors within 24 hours: Delhi HC
The Delhi High Court has told the MCD and NDMC to issue seizure details to street vendors within 24 hours and record seizures on video. The order reinforces statutory safeguards for vendors while pushing civic bodies to maintain clear, accountable records.
The Delhi High Court has directed the MCD and the NDMC to issue seizure memos to street vendors within 24 hours of seizing their goods and to videograph the seizure process. The court said the memos must include the date of seizure, the list of goods taken, the shelf numbers where the items are kept, any penalty or fine to be paid, and details of the officer concerned.
The order was passed on September 10 by a bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Vikas Mahajan while hearing a petition on seizures of street vendors' goods by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and the New Delhi Municipal Council in cases of violations by vendors.
The petitioner organisation, Rehri Patri Ekta Manch, told the court that whenever such seizures are carried out, no seizure memo is prepared by the MCD and NDMC and vendors are not given a list of the goods seized. The plea said that only a receipt for payment of fine is issued in the evening after the seizure.
Counsel for the MCD and NDMC submitted that the usual process is to first carry out the seizure and prepare the seizure memo later in the evening. They said that if officials prepare the memo on the spot, other vendors in the area will come to know about the action and escape seizure after committing violations.
The NDMC's counsel also told the court that the authority maintains a proper warehouse for storing seized goods and that vendors' items are kept on specific shelves. He said the relevant shelf number is mentioned in the receipt given to the vendor, and that the goods are released after payment of the fine.
He added that videography or photography of the seizure is also done by officials, depending on the resources available at the time.
In its order, the high court noted that both the MCD and the NDMC are expected to follow Section 19 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. The provision requires that when a seizure is carried out, a list of the goods seized must be prepared and a copy must be given to the vendor.
The court said, "Accordingly, considering the difficulties expressed by the authorities that if seizure memos are prepared on spot, other vendors who are in the area tend to escape action, the MCD and NDMC are permitted to issue seizure memos, in accordance with law within an outer limit of 24 hours from the seizure."
It also directed the MCD to carry out videography and photography during seizures, as is being done by the NDMC.
On the issue of the constitution of Town Vending Committee-II, counsel for the MCD said 23 members had been elected so far. He told the court that the list of nominated or designated members from various zones was still awaited and, once received, the names would be sent to the Delhi government for notification of TVC-II.
The court asked for the process to be expedited and disposed of the petition.

The use of coal to generate electricity on the US grid has been plunging for nearly two decades, and the first Trump administration was unable to affect the trend. So his second administration has attempted more aggressive interventions to prop up coal use. One of its most direct means of doing so is to order coal plants that were scheduled to close to remain open, even if there is no need for them.
The administration’s justification for these orders is a statute that allows the Department of Energy (DOE) to declare an emergency in the case of wartime or a sudden shortfall in generation. A number of parties, including states where coal plants have been slated to close, have challenged this declaration. And on Friday, in the first of these cases to make its way through the courts, the declaration was judged to be contrary to the statute. While this only affects a single coal plant in Michigan, the reasoning of the decision will apply to every coal plant closure that has been blocked by the DOE.
No emergency
The decision was issued by a unanimous three-judge panel from the DC Circuit’s Court of Appeals. It focuses on the J.H. Campbell Generating Plant, which was scheduled to close last year but has been kept open by a total of five emergency declarations by the DOE, each limited to 90 days by the Federal Power Act. At issue was section 202(c) of that Act, which allows the DOE to declare emergencies when the US is at war or when “an emergency exists by reason of a sudden increase in the demand for electric energy, or a shortage of electric energy.”

Brics Summit: PM Modi’s bilateral talks put security, trade in focus
Modi and Marcos agreed to enhance India-Philippines cooperation in defense, trade, and security at the Brics Summit, addressing regional issues together.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Philippines President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr agreed to expand cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment during a meeting on the margins of the Brics Summit on Sunday.
The Philippines participated in the summit as the current chair of Asean, providing an opportunity for the two leaders to review bilateral ties. The Philippines is a key partner for India in the Asean grouping and shared concerns over China’s actions across the region have fostered closer strategic and security cooperation between the two countries.
The leaders expressed satisfaction at progress in bilateral cooperation across all areas and agreed to deepen and expand collaboration in defence, security, trade, investment, space, railway infrastructure, fintech, education, tourism, technology, and people-to-people ties, the external affairs ministry said in a readout.
Deep Dive
Modi and Marcos also discussed regional and global issues and reiterated their commitment to strengthen cooperation across all areas of the bilateral strategic partnership.
“We reviewed the growing momentum in the India-Philippines strategic partnership,” Modi said on social media, adding that focus areas in the discussions included economic linkages, technology, trade and space.
Modi held a separate meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and reviewed cooperation in diverse areas. They also exchanged views on global issues and agreed to maintain close coordination at multilateral forums, the ministry said.
Modi said on social media that he and Ramaphosa reviewed the India-South Africa strategic partnership, including the India-SACU trade agreement, mining and critical minerals, infrastructure, food security, digital public infrastructure and emerging technologies.
“We will work closely for Africa’s progress, the priorities of the Global South and a more balanced global order,” Modi said.
Modi also held meetings with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Ugandan vice president Jessica Rose Epel Alupo, Nigerian vice president Kashim Shettima Mustapha, Burundi President Évariste Ndayishimiye, who is also chairperson of the African Union, and reviewed bilateral ties.
Modi and Tokayev reviewed bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals and emerging technologies, and exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments.
They agreed to strengthen the bilateral strategic partnership for peace, stability and development in the region.
Modi and Alupo reviewed ties between India and Uganda and emphasised the need to enhance cooperation in priority areas through technology partnerships, investment facilitation, and private sector collaboration. They also called for closer bilateral engagement to champion the voice of the Global South.
Modi and Mustapha reviewed the India-Nigeria relationship and discussions focussed on key areas such as trade, investment, defence, energy partnership, agriculture, health and digital technologies. Modi and Mustapha also discussed regional and global matters, including priorities and concerns of the Global South.
They emphasised the importance of strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums and working together for a more representative, inclusive and multipolar global order. Modi highlighted India’s commitment to deepen engagement with Africa, and Mustapha appreciated India’s contribution to capacity building and economic development in Nigeria.
Modi and Ndayishimiye stressed that the India-African Union partnership is a key pillar of cooperation within the Global South. They discussed the early convening of the India-Africa Forum Summit.
Modi commended the African Union leadership for combating the Ebola outbreak, and Ndayishimiye appreciated New Delhi’s medical support to Africa CDC to help in mitigating the outbreak.
